data.title: AI | David Baszucki Says Roblox AI Content Surged as Daily Users Fell 9%
data.description: Roblox CEO David Baszucki said AI-fueled content on the platform surged over the last three months, according to Bloomberg. Daily active users fell 9% last quarter and bookings declined 12% as the company rolled out tougher child-safety measures.

data.title: AI | Peter Singlehurst Says Anthropic’s Technical Edge Appeals to Long-Term Investors
data.description: Anthropic’s technical expertise, innovation and efficient use of compute set it apart in the AI landscape, said Peter Singlehurst, head of Baillie Gifford’s Private Companies Team, according to Bloomberg. Singlehurst said Anthropic’s governance structure, which gives its seven founders voting control, is good for long-term investors. He discussed the company with Ed Ludlow on “Bloomberg Tech.”

data.title: Godongwana Says Revised South African GDP Creates Fiscal Room
data.description: South African Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana said an upward revision to gross domestic product, following a regular recalculation of how the economy is measured, creates fiscal headroom for the country, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Dallas Fed President Lorie K. Logan: Fed Needs at Least Two More 25-Basis-Point Hikes
data.description: According to Jin10, Dallas Fed President Lorie K. Logan said the Fed needs at least two more rate hikes of 25 basis points each.

data.title: STOCKS | Oil Majors Post $56.3 Billion Windfall as Fuel Prices Surge
data.description: Exxon Mobil, Chevron, BP, Shell and TotalEnergies exceeded third-quarter expectations, reporting combined adjusted net income of $56.3 billion as conflicts in the Persian Gulf and Russia drove refining results to record highs, Bloomberg reported.

data.title: Gencom, White Bridge Capital Pay About $300 Million for Miami InterContinental
data.description: Gencom and White Bridge Capital bought the InterContinental hotel in downtown Miami for about $300 million, according to Bloomberg. The purchase marks the companies’ third joint hospitality deal in the past year.

data.title: STOCKS | Aspen Neuroscience Drops 2% After $140.6 Million US IPO
data.description: Aspen Neuroscience Inc., a Gilead-backed clinical-stage cell therapy developer, fell 2% after raising about $140.6 million in a US initial public offering, Bloomberg reported.

data.title: Deutsche Bank's AI Dollar Warning Could Hit Bitcoin, Gold and Stocks
data.description: Deutsche Bank warned that an AI-led selloff could weaken the U.S. dollar alongside stocks, challenging the dollar’s usual safe-haven role when equities fall. Foreign investors own more than $20 trillion in U.S. shares, with about 90% of that value attributed to price appreciation, according to BeInCrypto. Deutsche Bank’s George Saravelos said falling U.S. real yields alongside weaker stocks and the dollar would signal markets cutting AI spending forecasts; Friday’s trading did not show that mix, as the dollar edged higher. Bitcoin and gold, both priced in dollars, could also be affected.

data.title: Tether Reports $191.5 Billion in Q3 Reserves and $1.5 Billion in Operating Profit
data.description:
Tether International, S.A. de C.V. released an assurance report prepared by BDO covering the third quarter of 2026, with data as of September 30. According to Odaily, Tether’s reserves totaled $191.5 billion at quarter-end, including $132.4 billion in direct and indirect U.S. Treasury holdings.

USD₮ issuance remained around $184 billion through the first three quarters, while cumulative net operating profit reached $4.5 billion. Third-quarter net operating profit was $1.5 billion, unchanged from the second quarter; U.S. Treasury securities and reverse repurchase agreements generated most of the revenue.

As of September 30, Tether reported total assets of $191.451 billion and total liabilities of $183.496 billion, leaving assets $7.955 billion above liabilities. Excess reserves increased to about $7.95 billion from $4.1 billion at the end of the second quarter.

data.title: St. Louis Fed President Alberto G. Musalem: Earlier Rate Hikes Could Reduce Economic Shock Risk
data.description: St. Louis Fed President Alberto G. Musalem said monetary policy and overall financial conditions remain accommodative, while inflation is still too high. According to Odaily, Musalem said inflation is unlikely to ease without Fed action and that raising rates earlier could reduce the risk of a shock to the broader economy.

data.title: AFT Sues Trump Administration Over Student Loan Forgiveness Delays
data.description: According to CNBC, the American Federation of Teachers sued the Trump administration Friday, alleging officials unlawfully blocked student loan forgiveness for tens of thousands of eligible borrowers. The lawsuit alleges Education Secretary Linda McMahon mismanaged the Public Service Loan Forgiveness program by miscounting payment timelines and failing to credit qualifying service. It also challenges delays in the PSLF Buyback program; 88,000 borrowers were still awaiting decisions as of the spring, according to a court filing. The Education Department said it was correcting coding errors from the Biden administration that had led to inaccurate payment counts.

data.title: Grand Canyon Inn Operator Files for Chapter 11 Bankruptcy Protection
data.description: Grand Canyon Hotel Services LLC, operator of the 101-room Grand Canyon Inn in Valle, Arizona, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on October 29 to restructure its debt. According to Sina Finance, court records show the company listed assets and liabilities in the range of $1 million to $10 million; it also operates seven other hotels across the United States. A 2025 wildfire that destroyed Grand Canyon Lodge and an August 29, 2026, flash flood damaged park infrastructure, while hotel occupancy and revenue in the area fell. The Grand Canyon Inn was listed for sale on July 14, 2026, for $7.95 million. A planned renovation of the company’s 28-room Grand Canyon Motel and construction of a 50-space RV park have an uncertain future as the bankruptcy proceeds.

data.title: Elon Musk's $119 Billion Terafab Faces Payoff Question Without Outside Customers
data.description: Elon Musk said Terafab is going well, but the planned Tesla and SpaceX chip plant in Texas, estimated to cost up to $119 billion, has no outside customers to share the bill. Korean supplier remarks cited by The Elec describe U.S. replies within 30 minutes to an hour, according to BeInCrypto. Tesla and SpaceX procurement staff visited about 10 Korean booths at SEMICON West, and more than half of those firms are discussing potential supply items. Terafab aims to produce 1 million wafers monthly within a decade; Intel joined as a technology partner in the spring. No fab has produced that volume solely for its owners, and Musk has never run a chip plant.

data.title: Binance News Update | Richard Teng: Binance Will Cover All Hacked Losses With Company Funds, $6.34 Billion Reserved and $5 Billion Already Held in the Affected Tokens
data.description: Binance CEO Richard Teng said the exchange will cover all losses from its security incident with company funds, having reserved more than $6.34 billion, $5 billion of which is already held in the exact tokens affected, including USDC, USDT, BTC, ETH and BNB. In a video message to users posted on X on Friday, October 30, Teng said customer funds were not affected, and shared new details about how the attack was carried out.“I want to be clear: we are committed to covering all hacked losses through our company funds,” Teng said. “Your assets are safe.”Built for the Long TermTeng said Binance can absorb a loss of this size immediately because of how it manages its own earnings. “Binance has always been built for the long term,” he said. “Most of what we earn from day-to-day operations is held in crypto assets. We have kept a lot of them in the company, and reinvested them — into the business, and into security. Because we believe in crypto, and in the long-term value of this industry.”That is why most of the affected tokens are already covered, Teng said. Binance is buying the remaining amount through market and OTC channels, and “the good news is that we are recovering stolen assets for users.”Customer Funds Were Not AffectedTeng addressed the question many users have been asking: how Binance can show their assets were not affected. “We never use any customer funds, so they are not impacted,” he said. “What was affected in this incident was Binance’s own hot wallet.”Under Binance’s security setup, most user assets are held in cold wallets and moved to a hot wallet only when a user makes a withdrawal. Teng encouraged concerned users to check their account balances and contact customer service with any questions.How the Attack Was Carried OutTeng said the attack was complex and not carried out by one person. Binance’s first findings pointed to a compromised laptop, and further investigation has uncovered additional points of breach.The attackers used EIP-7702, an Ethereum standard that lets a wallet delegate its execution to smart-contract code, to obtain on-chain execution approval over a Binance hot wallet. “That delegation did not pass through our normal approval controls,” Teng said. “That’s why we need to pause the withdrawal service to investigate, rebuild and retest the entire infrastructure system.”The attackers also used a self-destruct mechanism that “destroyed tooling and traces as they went,” he said, making the investigation harder. Binance is working with law enforcement, blockchain intelligence firms, token issuers and other exchanges to trace and recover the stolen funds, and about $3 billion has already been frozen with partners’ help. “We will do everything within our power to ensure that these bad actors will be held accountable,” Teng said.Withdrawals Expected Before SundayBinance is rebuilding its withdrawal service and will not switch it back on until it passes rigorous testing. “We are very hopeful that users will be able to withdraw prior to our Sunday deadline, which is on track to be within 40 hours,” Teng said.At the same time, Binance is running a full security review across the company, covering “endpoints, cloud, key management, signing. Everything.”Proof of Reserves by MondayOnce the remaining token purchases are complete, Binance will verify user assets through its Proof of Reserves. A full report is due by Monday, with an initial view possibly before then.Teng thanked industry partners, law enforcement and, “most of all,” users for their patience. “We will weather this storm,” he said. “Thank you for the support, and stay safe.”

data.title: Bergeron Seeks Removal of Ethan Allen CEO Kathwari, Wants Ward as Successor
data.description: DGB Investments founder Douglas Bergeron is pushing for major changes at Ethan Allen Interiors Inc., calling for CEO and Chairman Farooq Kathwari to be removed and replaced by Stefanie Tsen Ward, Bloomberg reported. Bergeron made the remarks on Bloomberg Open Interest.
